title: Effects of early ortho-geriatric co-management on the treatment of older orthopaedic patients with elective surgery - a prospective randomised controlled intervention study
summary:
Demographic change is leading to an increase in "geriatric" patients, not only in trauma surgery but also in orthopedics. The problems associated with this, such as multimorbidity and polypharmacy, pose major challenges for physicians working in the field of surgery. Several clinical studies have already shown that close geriatric-trauma surgery collaboration has a positive effect on the perioperative care of the elderly. 
Whether close geriatric-orthopedic collaboration also has a positive effect is still completely unclear. A close cooperation model with the Center for Geriatric Medicine of the Helios Klinikum Bonn/Rhein-Sieg has already been in place at the Clinic for Orthopedics and Trauma Surgery of the University of Bonn since May 2017. Here, orthopedic surgeons and geriatricians jointly care for elderly orthopedic patients. In the present study, such a geriatric-orthopedic care model, in which orthopedists and geriatricians share the treatment responsibility for planned surgical interventions already in the early preoperative phase, is to be evaluated for a specific orthopedic patient collective with regard to its effects.

The aim of the study is to significantly improve the functional status, measured as Short Physical Performance Battery (SPPB), at 4 months postoperatively by geriatric-orthopedic co-management compared to a comparison group ("usual care").

interventions.name: With geriatrician and CGA-guided intervention: intervention group (early preoperative involvement of geriatrician with CGA-guided intervention including postoperative further specialist follow-up in the form of daily visits by the geriatrician).
Without geriatrician: control group "usual care" (no preoperative involvement of the geriatrician. However, inclusion may be permitted in the postoperative course if medically necessary).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Patients of the clinic for orthopedics
- ≥70 years
- Elective major procedures:
o primary knee or hip arthroplasty
o Knee/hip arthroplasty exchange (aseptic/septic)
o Spinal interventions
Selective decompression (spinal intervention without instrumentation)
One- and two-segment spondylodesis
tri- and multisegmental spondylodesis
Kyphoplasty
- Geriatric-type multimorbidity (≥3 diseases)
- Polypharmacy (≥5 medications)
- ISAR ≥2
Exclusion criteria:
- (Planned) geriatric complex treatment (if necessary also exclusion of patients in the course!)
- Disease in final stage
- Severe/advanced dementia (MMSE<10)
- Lack of consent (self or by proxy or guardian)
- Lack of guardian or authorized representative with MMSE < 18 (up to an MMSE of 18 - i.e. a slight cognitive impairment - it can usually still be assumed that there is capacity to act)
